Finding: Public booking idempotency is read-before-write without a database uniqueness constraint
Evidence: public_booking.py:699-704; audit/2026-09-03/probe-results.json persisted two rows once with one key
Customer/Business Impact: A retry or two app instances can create duplicate bookings and downstream charges
Required Remediation: Add scoped UNIQUE constraint; transactional insert/upsert; request-hash conflict detection; stable replay response; multi-instance PostgreSQL race test

Finding: No production-equivalent proof of zero duplicate or lost financial outcomes under load
Evidence: Only mock/unit tests and one-process HTTP probe exist
Customer/Business Impact: Payments cannot be trusted at scale or through failover
Required Remediation: Run signed webhook/payment/release/refund races on production-parity PostgreSQL and reconcile provider plus internal ledgers

Finding: One process-global mutex serializes nearly every matched API route
Customer/Business Impact: Concurrent booking login tracking and payment requests queue behind one operation
Required Remediation: Use per-request connections from a bounded pool; remove global lock; add row/transaction locking by business aggregate

Finding: One process-global database connection serves all request threads
Customer/Business Impact: Connection failure affects all traffic and prevents horizontal-safe concurrency
Required Remediation: Adopt pooler and request-scoped transaction/session lifecycle with health and saturation metrics

Finding: Current deployment describes one free web instance
Customer/Business Impact: One process or host failure can take down the API; cold starts violate latency
Required Remediation: Deploy at least two paid instances across failure domains behind a health-aware load balancer with autoscaling

Finding: Current database is a free single declared database with no evidenced HA/PITR policy
Customer/Business Impact: Database failure can exceed RTO/RPO and stop all bookings/payments
Required Remediation: Use managed HA PostgreSQL with PITR encrypted backups pooling and tested restore/failover

Finding: Public rate limit is 20 POSTs/minute per process-observed socket IP
Evidence: server.py:2163-2177 and 2936; mixed 100-user run returned sixteen 429s
Customer/Business Impact: Users behind a corporate NAT or load balancer can block each other; replicas enforce inconsistent limits
Required Remediation: Move to shared limiter keyed by verified client/user plus trusted proxy-aware IP; separate endpoint budgets and Retry-After

Finding: Mixed 100-user local workload fails latency and error gates
Customer/Business Impact: Legitimate concurrent users cannot complete bookings predictably
Required Remediation: Fix limiter and serialization then run production-parity 100-user gate until it passes twice

Finding: Read-only workload reaches its first formal failure at 1000 concurrent clients
Customer/Business Impact: No verified runway to required 2500-10000 user stages
Required Remediation: Horizontalize services and run distributed load generation through every stage

Finding: No infrastructure-level durable queue and isolated worker deployment is configured
Evidence: render.yaml has only one web service and database
Customer/Business Impact: Slow notification document payment reconciliation or report work can consume request capacity
Required Remediation: Provision durable queue dead-letter path and independently autoscaled workers; use transactional outbox

Finding: Managed PostgreSQL restore is a printed playbook not an executed test
Customer/Business Impact: RTO and RPO for production data are unknown
Required Remediation: Perform destructive restore into isolated target; capture timestamps counts hashes and reconciliation

Finding: No systemwide metrics distributed tracing business SLO dashboards or paging rules are configured
Evidence: Access logs contain per-request duration only; no metrics stack in deployment
Customer/Business Impact: Failures can remain invisible while bookings or payments are wrong
Required Remediation: Instrument OpenTelemetry/metrics; add booking/payment/queue/database dashboards alerts and runbooks

Finding: Location pings use the main relational database and MAX(seq)+1
Customer/Business Impact: High-rate GPS writes can contend with booking/payment workloads and duplicate sequence values
Required Remediation: Use stream ingestion and time-series/location store; database-enforced sequence/idempotency; adaptive frequency

Finding: No 8-24 hour soak mature-data or queue-recovery result exists
Evidence: No k6/Locust tool installed and no performance workflow before this audit
Customer/Business Impact: Leaks buildup token expiry and long-running degradation remain unknown
Required Remediation: Execute peak soak with mature data and post-run reconciliation in dedicated environment

Finding: No failover chaos or external-provider outage exercise has been executed
Evidence: No HA environment; external controls are code-level mocks
Customer/Business Impact: System may show false success or stick transactions during dependency failure
Required Remediation: Inject app DB cache queue map payment SMS email and storage failures and prove recovery

Finding: No managed shared cache/session/rate-limit service is configured
Customer/Business Impact: Reference reads repeat work and horizontal instances cannot share limiter/session state
Required Remediation: Provision Redis/Valkey for non-authoritative data with outage behavior tests

Finding: Schema migration runs in every container startup command
Customer/Business Impact: Concurrent rollout can race migrations and couple recovery to schema change
Required Remediation: Run one controlled migration job; use expand/contract migrations and rollback checks

Finding: Auto-deploy is enabled without evidenced canary/blue-green or automatic rollback
Customer/Business Impact: A failed deployment can affect all traffic at once
Required Remediation: Add staged deployment readiness business canaries and rollback conditions

Finding: Documents and POD storage are not backed by an evidenced object-store malware-scan design
Evidence: No object storage service in deployment blueprint
Customer/Business Impact: Uploads can burden the app/database and recovery controls are unclear
Required Remediation: Use private encrypted object storage signed URLs scanning versioning and retention

Finding: Capacity and cost forecasts are engineering assumptions rather than approved business inputs
Customer/Business Impact: Infrastructure could be overbuilt or undersized
Required Remediation: Product Finance Operations and Growth approve volumes RTO RPO SLO and budget; recalibrate with analytics
